paragraphs.text: וְאִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֣ת מִנְּשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי־הַ֠נְּבִיאִים צָעֲקָ֨ה אֶל־אֱלִישָׁ֜ע לֵאמֹ֗ר עַבְדְּךָ֤ אִישִׁי֙ מֵ֔ת וְאַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּ֣י עַבְדְּךָ֔ הָיָ֥ה יָרֵ֖א אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וְהַ֨נֹּשֶׁ֔ה בָּ֗א לָקַ֜חַת אֶת־שְׁנֵ֧י יְלָדַ֛י ל֖וֹ לַעֲבָדִֽים׃

i18n.en: Now a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, "Your servant my husband is dead; and you know that your servant feared YHWH; and the creditor has come to take my two children to be his slaves."

notes.official:
Names in this chapter: Elisha = Elisha; Shunem = Shunem; the Shunammite = the Shunammite; Gechazi = Gehazi; Karmel = Carmel; Ba'al-Shalishah = Baal-shalishah; Gilgal is kept in its English form (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`).

*ʾiššâ ʾaḥaṯ minnəšê ḇənê-hannəḇîʾîm* 'a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets': the prophetic groups included married men with households (`bene-ha-neviim-sons-of-the-prophets-kings`; central `navi-first-occurrence-abraham`). *wəhannōšeh bāʾ lāqaḥaṯ ʾeṯ-šənê yəlāḏay lô laʿăḇāḏîm* 'and the creditor has come to take my two children to be his slaves': debt-slavery of children is regulated in Ex 21:2-11 and Deut 15:12-18 and attested across the ANE (cf. Neh 5:5). The miracle story is a doublet of Eliyahu's at Tzarfat (1 Kgs 17:8-16), as the next one (vv 8-37) is of 17:17-24.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלֶ֤יהָ אֱלִישָׁע֙ מָ֣ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ הַגִּ֣ידִי לִ֔י מַה־יֶּשׁ־לכי [לָ֖ךְ] בַּבָּ֑יִת וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אֵ֣ין לְשִׁפְחָתְךָ֥ כֹל֙ בַּבַּ֔יִת כִּ֖י אִם־אָס֥וּךְ שָֽׁמֶן׃

i18n.en: And Elisha said to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" And she said, "Your maidservant has nothing at all in the house except a pot of oil."

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *lky* (archaic 2nd feminine singular suffix) / Qere *lāḵ* 'to you'; the Qere is translated. The archaic feminine forms *-kî* / *ʾattî* recur in this chapter's Ketiv (vv 2, 3, 7, 16, 23); they are a known feature of the Elisha narratives, often explained as northern dialect or archaic usage (Rendsburg, *Israelian Hebrew in the Book of Kings*, 2002), and do not change the sense (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

*ʾāsûḵ šāmen* 'a pot of oil' (ASV): *ʾāsûḵ* occurs only here, from *swk* 'anoint', so perhaps a small flask or jar of anointing oil; the ASV word is kept.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכִ֨י שַׁאֲלִי־לָ֤ךְ כֵּלִים֙ מִן־הַח֔וּץ מֵאֵ֖ת כָּל־שכנכי [שְׁכֵנָ֑יִךְ] כֵּלִ֥ים רֵקִ֖ים אַל־תַּמְעִֽיטִי׃

i18n.en: Then he said, "Go, borrow vessels for yourself from outside, from all your neighbors — empty vessels; do not borrow too few.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *šknky* (archaic 2nd feminine singular suffix) / Qere *šəḵēnāyiḵ* 'your neighbors' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`; see v 2). *ʾal-tamʿîṭî* 'do not borrow too few' (lit. 'do not make few').

paragraphs.text: וּבָ֗את וְסָגַ֤רְתְּ הַדֶּ֙לֶת֙ בַּעֲדֵ֣ךְ וּבְעַד־בָּנַ֔יִךְ וְיָצַ֕קְתְּ עַ֥ל כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְהַמָּלֵ֖א תַּסִּֽיעִי׃

i18n.en: And you shall go in and shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour into all these vessels; and set aside what is full."

notes.official: *wəsāḡart haddeleṯ baʿăḏēḵ* 'and shut the door behind you': the miracle takes place behind a closed door, as does the raising of the boy (vv 21, 33).

paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ מֵֽאִתּ֔וֹ וַתִּסְגֹּ֣ר הַדֶּ֔לֶת בַּעֲדָ֖הּ וּבְעַ֣ד בָּנֶ֑יהָ הֵ֛ם מַגִּשִׁ֥ים אֵלֶ֖יהָ וְהִ֥יא מיצקת [מוֹצָֽקֶת׃]

i18n.en: So she went from him and shut the door behind her and her sons; they were bringing the vessels to her, and she was pouring.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *myṣqt* (Hiphil participle) / Qere *môṣāqeṯ* (Hophal-type participle), both 'pouring'; the Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). In the Hebrew text field the verse-final sof pasuq sits inside the bracketed Qere ([מוֹצָֽקֶת׃]); this is how the source edition encodes a Qere at verse end and is kept as delivered (also 17:31).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ כִּמְלֹ֣את הַכֵּלִ֗ים וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל־בְּנָהּ֙ הַגִּ֨ישָׁה אֵלַ֥י עוֹד֙ כֶּ֔לִי וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אֵ֥ין ע֖וֹד כֶּ֑לִי וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד הַשָּֽׁמֶן׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." And he said to her, "There is not another vessel." And the oil stopped.

notes.official: *wayyaʿămōḏ haššāmen* 'And the oil stopped' (lit. 'stood').

paragraphs.text: וַתָּבֹ֗א וַתַּגֵּד֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכִי֙ מִכְרִ֣י אֶת־הַשֶּׁ֔מֶן וְשַׁלְּמִ֖י אֶת־נשיכי [נִשְׁיֵ֑ךְ] וְאַ֣תְּ בניכי [וּבָנַ֔יִךְ] תִֽחְיִ֖י בַּנּוֹתָֽר׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Then she came and told the man of the Elohim. And he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debt; and you and your sons shall live on the rest."

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere, two readings: Ketiv *nšyky* / Qere *nišyēḵ* 'your debt' (archaic suffix); Ketiv *bnyky* 'your sons' / Qere *ûḇānayiḵ* 'and your sons' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

*ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm* 'the man of the Elohim': the Hebrew article is kept, as everywhere in Kings (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`; also vv 16, 21, 22, 25 twice, 27 twice, 40, 42; anarthrous at v 9). *tiḥyî bannôṯār* 'you shall live on the rest'. The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) closes the episode.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אֶל־שׁוּנֵ֗ם וְשָׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַתַּחֲזֶק־בּ֖וֹ לֶאֱכָל־לָ֑חֶם וַֽיְהִי֙ מִדֵּ֣י עָבְר֔וֹ יָסֻ֥ר שָׁ֖מָּה לֶאֱכָל־לָֽחֶם׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass one day that Elisha passed over to Shunem, and a great woman was there; and she urged him to eat bread. And so it was, whenever he passed by, he would turn aside there to eat bread.

notes.official: *wayəhî hayyôm* 'And it came to pass one day' (also vv 11, 18). *ʾiššâ ḡəḏôlâ* 'a great woman' (ASV): 'great' in social standing, i.e. wealthy or prominent (NJPS 'a wealthy woman'); the literal adjective is kept. *wattaḥăzeq-bô* 'and she urged him' (lit. 'took hold of him'). Shunem lies in the Yizre'el valley, about 25 km from Mount Karmel (v 25).

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־אִישָׁ֔הּ הִנֵּה־נָ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ אֱלֹהִ֖ים קָד֣וֹשׁ ה֑וּא עֹבֵ֥ר עָלֵ֖ינוּ תָּמִֽיד׃

i18n.en: And she said to her husband, "Behold now, I know that this is a holy man of Elohim who passes by us continually.

notes.official: *kî ʾîš ʾĕlōhîm qāḏôš hûʾ* 'that this is a holy man of Elohim': the title is anarthrous here, the only such case in the chapter, and is rendered 'a ... man of Elohim' (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`). *qāḏôš* 'holy' is used of a person only rarely (Num 16:7; Ps 106:16).

paragraphs.text: נַֽעֲשֶׂה־נָּ֤א עֲלִיַּת־קִיר֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה וְנָשִׂ֨ים ל֥וֹ שָׁ֛ם מִטָּ֥ה וְשֻׁלְחָ֖ן וְכִסֵּ֣א וּמְנוֹרָ֑ה וְהָיָ֛ה בְּבֹא֥וֹ אֵלֵ֖ינוּ יָס֥וּר שָֽׁמָּה׃

i18n.en: Let us make, I pray, a little chamber on the wall, and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a seat, and a lampstand; and it shall be, when he comes to us, that he will turn aside there."

notes.official: *ʿăliyyaṯ-qîr qəṭannâ* 'a little chamber on the wall' (ASV): an upper room, probably a roof chamber with walls of its own (NRSV 'a small roof chamber with walls'); cf. the *ʿăliyyâ* of 1 Kgs 17:19, 23. The furnishing (bed, table, seat, lampstand) is that of an honoured guest's room.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם וַיָּ֣בֹא שָׁ֑מָּה וַיָּ֥סַר אֶל־הָעֲלִיָּ֖ה וַיִּשְׁכַּב־שָֽׁמָּה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass one day that he came there, and he turned aside into the upper chamber and lay down there.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־גֵּחֲזִ֣י נַעֲר֔וֹ קְרָ֖א לַשּׁוּנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את וַיִּקְרָא־לָ֔הּ וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And he said to Gechazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite." And he called her, and she stood before him.

notes.official: *geḥăzî naʿărô* 'Gechazi his servant'. *naʿar* is used for the prophet's attendant (vv 12, 25; also the reapers' and the household's servants, vv 19, 22, 24) and for the boy (vv 29-35); the English follows the ASV, 'servant' for the attendant and 'child' for the boy, and the commentary notes the shared noun. The name is spelled *gēḥăzî* here and at v 31 and *gêḥăzî* at vv 14, 25, 27, 29, 36, an orthographic variant rendered identically (Gechazi = Gehazi). *qərāʾ laššûnammîṯ hazzōʾṯ* 'Call this Shunammite': the gentilic of Shunem, as at 1 Kgs 1:3.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אֱמָר־נָ֣א אֵלֶיהָ֮ הִנֵּ֣ה חָרַ֣דְתְּ ׀ אֵלֵינוּ֮ אֶת־כָּל־הַחֲרָדָ֣ה הַזֹּאת֒ מֶ֚ה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ֔ךְ הֲיֵ֤שׁ לְדַבֶּר־לָךְ֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ א֖וֹ אֶל־שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֑א וַתֹּ֕אמֶר בְּת֥וֹךְ עַמִּ֖י אָנֹכִ֥י יֹשָֽׁבֶת׃

i18n.en: And he said to him, "Say now to her, 'Behold, you have been careful for us with all this care; what is to be done for you? Is there anything to be spoken for you to the king, or to the captain of the host?'" And she said, "I dwell among my own people."

notes.official: *hinnēh ḥāraḏt ʾēlênû ʾeṯ-kol-haḥărāḏâ hazzōʾṯ* 'Behold, you have been careful for us with all this care' (ASV): *ḥrd* is 'tremble', here 'take anxious trouble' for someone, with a cognate accusative. *śar haṣṣāḇāʾ* 'the captain of the host' (ASV; kept as at 1 Kgs 1:19, and for the lexical link with *ṣəḇāʾ haššāmayim*, 2 Kgs 17:16). *bəṯôḵ ʿammî ʾānōḵî yōšāḇeṯ* 'I dwell among my own people': she needs no patron at court.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר וּמֶ֖ה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ֑הּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּיחֲזִ֗י אֲבָ֛ל בֵּ֥ן אֵֽין־לָ֖הּ וְאִישָׁ֥הּ זָקֵֽן׃

i18n.en: And he said, "What then is to be done for her?" And Gechazi said, "Truly, she has no son, and her husband is old."

notes.official: *ʾăḇāl bēn ʾên-lāh wəʾîšāh zāqēn* 'Truly, she has no son, and her husband is old': the motif of the childless woman with an old husband recalls Sarah (Gen 18:11-12), to which v 16 alludes.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר קְרָא־לָ֑הּ וַיִּקְרָא־לָ֔הּ וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד בַּפָּֽתַח׃

i18n.en: And he said, "Call her." And he called her, and she stood in the doorway.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לַמּוֹעֵ֤ד הַזֶּה֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה אתי [אַ֖תְּ] חֹבֶ֣קֶת בֵּ֑ן וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אַל־אֲדֹנִי֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אַל־תְּכַזֵּ֖ב בְּשִׁפְחָתֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And he said, "At this appointed time, when the season comes around, you shall be embracing a son." And she said, "No, my lord, man of the Elohim, do not lie to your maidservant."

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *ʾty* (archaic 2nd feminine singular pronoun) / Qere *ʾatt* 'you' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

*lammôʿēḏ hazzeh kāʿēṯ ḥayyâ ʾatt ḥōḇeqeṯ bēn* 'At this appointed time, when the season comes around, you shall be embracing a son'. *kāʿēṯ ḥayyâ* occurs only here, at v 17 and in the announcement to Sarah (Gen 18:10, 14), and *lammôʿēḏ* recalls Gen 18:14 and 17:21; the corpus rendering is used so that the allusion stays visible (central `ka-et-chayah-time-of-life`, whose rationale already names this verse). *ʾal-təḵazzēḇ bəšip̄ḥāṯeḵā* 'do not lie to your maidservant' (cf. Sarah's laugh, Gen 18:12-15). 'man of the Elohim' (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן לַמּוֹעֵ֤ד הַזֶּה֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יהָ אֱלִישָֽׁע׃

i18n.en: And the woman conceived and bore a son at that appointed time, when the season came around, as Elisha had spoken to her.

notes.official: *lammôʿēḏ hazzeh kāʿēṯ ḥayyâ* 'at that appointed time, when the season came around' (central `ka-et-chayah-time-of-life`; see v 16).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּגְדַּ֖ל הַיָּ֑לֶד וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיֵּצֵ֥א אֶל־אָבִ֖יו אֶל־הַקֹּצְרִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the child grew; and it came to pass one day that he went out to his father, to the reapers.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֶל־אָבִ֖יו רֹאשִׁ֣י ׀ רֹאשִׁ֑י וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־הַנַּ֔עַר שָׂאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־אִמּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he said to his father, "My head, my head!" And he said to the servant, "Carry him to his mother."

notes.official: *rōʾšî rōʾšî* 'My head, my head!': the symptoms (sudden headache in the field at harvest, death by noon) suggest sunstroke, as many commentators observe (Cogan and Tadmor, *II Kings*, AB 11, 1988); the text does not name a cause. *ʾel-hannaʿar* 'to the servant' (see v 12).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשָּׂאֵ֔הוּ וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־אִמּ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב עַל־בִּרְכֶּ֛יהָ עַד־הַֽצָּהֳרַ֖יִם וַיָּמֹֽת׃

i18n.en: And he carried him and brought him to his mother; and he sat on her knees until noon, and he died.

paragraphs.text: וַתַּ֙עַל֙ וַתַּשְׁכִּבֵ֔הוּ עַל־מִטַּ֖ת אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתִּסְגֹּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וַתֵּצֵֽא׃

i18n.en: And she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of the Elohim, and shut the door on him, and went out.

notes.official: *ʿal-miṭṭaṯ ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm* 'on the bed of the man of the Elohim': she lays the boy in the prophet's room and closes the door, keeping the death secret (vv 22-23) (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַתִּקְרָא֮ אֶל־אִישָׁהּ֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שִׁלְחָ֨ה נָ֥א לִי֙ אֶחָ֣ד מִן־הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְאַחַ֖ת הָאֲתֹנ֑וֹת וְאָר֛וּצָה עַד־אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וְאָשֽׁוּבָה׃

i18n.en: And she called to her husband and said, "Send me, I pray, one of the servants and one of the she-asses, that I may run to the man of the Elohim and come back."

notes.official: *wəʾārûṣâ ʿaḏ-ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm* 'that I may run to the man of the Elohim' (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`). *hāʾăṯōnôṯ* 'the she-asses' (ASV), the riding animals of a well-to-do household.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מַ֠דּוּעַ אתי [אַ֣תְּ] הלכתי [הֹלֶ֤כֶת] אֵלָיו֙ הַיּ֔וֹם לֹֽא־חֹ֖דֶשׁ וְלֹ֣א שַׁבָּ֑ת וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And he said, "Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath." And she said, "It shall be well."

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere, two readings: Ketiv *ʾty* / Qere *ʾatt* 'you', and Ketiv *hlkty* / Qere *hōleḵeṯ* 'going' (archaic 2nd feminine singular forms; `ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

*lōʾ-ḥōḏeš wəlōʾ šabbāṯ* 'It is neither new moon nor Sabbath': new moon and Sabbath were days on which one visited a prophet or sanctuary (Amos 8:5; Isa 1:13). *wattōʾmer šālôm* 'And she said, "It shall be well"': the single word *šālôm* is her answer here and at v 26 ('It is well'), and the three questions of v 26 are each *hăšālôm* 'Is it well?'. The ASV renders by context; the commentary records that one Hebrew word carries all five, and that she uses it to avoid disclosing the death.

paragraphs.text: וַֽתַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ הָֽאָת֔וֹן וַתֹּ֥אמֶר אֶֽל־נַעֲרָ֖הּ נְהַ֣ג וָלֵ֑ךְ אַל־תַּעֲצָר־לִ֣י לִרְכֹּ֔ב כִּ֖י אִם־אָמַ֥רְתִּי לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: Then she saddled the she-ass and said to her servant, "Drive, and go on; do not hold back the riding for me unless I tell you."

notes.official: *nəhaḡ wāleḵ* 'Drive, and go on': the servant runs beside the donkey and drives it. *ʾal-taʿăṣār-lî lirkōḇ* 'do not hold back the riding for me'.

paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֗לֶךְ וַתָּב֛וֹא אֶל־אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וַ֠יְהִי כִּרְא֨וֹת אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים אֹתָהּ֙ מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־גֵּיחֲזִ֣י נַעֲר֔וֹ הִנֵּ֖ה הַשּׁוּנַמִּ֥ית הַלָּֽז׃

i18n.en: So she went and came to the man of the Elohim at Mount Karmel. And it came to pass, when the man of the Elohim saw her at a distance, that he said to Gechazi his servant, "Behold, there is that Shunammite.

notes.official: *ʾel-har hakkarmel* 'at Mount Karmel', the scene of 1 Kgs 18 (Karmel = Carmel). *hinnēh haššûnammîṯ hallāz* 'Behold, there is that Shunammite' (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`).

paragraphs.text: עַתָּה֮ רֽוּץ־נָ֣א לִקְרָאתָהּ֒ וֶאֱמָר־לָ֗הּ הֲשָׁל֥וֹם לָ֛ךְ הֲשָׁל֥וֹם לְאִישֵׁ֖ךְ הֲשָׁל֣וֹם לַיָּ֑לֶד וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: Run now, I pray, to meet her, and say to her, 'Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?'" And she said, "It is well."

notes.official: *hăšālôm lāḵ hăšālôm ləʾîšēḵ hăšālôm layyeleḏ* 'Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?' *wattōʾmer šālôm* 'It is well' (see v 23).

paragraphs.text: וַתָּבֹ֞א אֶל־אִ֤ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־הָהָ֔ר וַֽתַּחֲזֵ֖ק בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ גֵּֽיחֲזִ֜י לְהָדְפָ֗הּ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים הַרְפֵּֽה־לָהּ֙ כִּֽי־נַפְשָׁ֣הּ מָֽרָה־לָ֔הּ וַֽיהוָה֙ הֶעְלִ֣ים מִמֶּ֔נִּי וְלֹ֥א הִגִּ֖יד לִֽי׃

i18n.en: And she came to the man of the Elohim at the mountain and caught hold of his feet. And Gechazi came near to push her away; but the man of the Elohim said, "Let her alone, for she is in bitter distress; and YHWH has hidden it from me and has not told me."

notes.official: *wattaḥăzēq bəraḡlāyw* 'and caught hold of his feet', a gesture of supplication. *kî-nap̄šāh mārâ-lāh* 'for she is in bitter distress' (ASV 'her soul is vexed within her'). *mar-nep̄eš* 'bitter of *nep̄eš*' is an idiom for deep distress (1 Sam 1:10; 22:2; Judg 18:25), and *nep̄eš* here is the person's inner life, not a separable soul; the Kings convention renders such idioms in plain English and keeps 'soul' out of the line (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`). Literally: 'her *nep̄eš* is bitter to her'. *wayhwh heʿlîm mimmennî* 'and YHWH has hidden it from me': the prophet's knowledge depends on revelation (contrast 5:26). 'the man of the Elohim', twice (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר הֲשָׁאַ֥לְתִּי בֵ֖ן מֵאֵ֣ת אֲדֹנִ֑י הֲלֹ֣א אָמַ֔רְתִּי לֹ֥א תַשְׁלֶ֖ה אֹתִֽי׃

i18n.en: Then she said, "Did I ask a son of my lord? Did I not say, 'Do not deceive me'?"

notes.official: *lōʾ ṯašleh ʾōṯî* 'Do not deceive me' (Hiphil of *šlh*, 'lead astray, raise false hopes'); she recalls v 16.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לְגֵיחֲזִ֜י חֲגֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֗יךָ וְקַ֨ח מִשְׁעַנְתִּ֣י בְיָדְךָ֮ וָלֵךְ֒ כִּֽי־תִמְצָ֥א אִישׁ֙ לֹ֣א תְבָרְכֶ֔נּוּ וְכִֽי־יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ אִ֖ישׁ לֹ֣א תַעֲנֶנּ֑וּ וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ מִשְׁעַנְתִּ֖י עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַנָּֽעַר׃

i18n.en: Then he said to Gechazi, "Gird up your loins, and take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet any man, do not greet him; and if any man greets you, do not answer him; and lay my staff on the face of the child."

notes.official: *ḥăḡōr māṯneḵā* 'Gird up your loins', tuck up the robe for running (1 Kgs 18:46). *lōʾ ṯəḇārəḵennû* 'do not greet him' (lit. 'bless him'): there is to be no delay. *wəśamtā mišʿanṯî ʿal-pənê hannaʿar* 'and lay my staff on the face of the child': the staff as an extension of the prophet's power, which fails (v 31).

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֵ֣ם הַנַּ֔עַר חַי־יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם־אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אַחֲרֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And the mother of the child said, "As YHWH lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." And he arose and followed her.

notes.official: *ḥay-YHWH wəḥê-nap̄šəḵā ʾim-ʾeʿezḇekkā* 'As YHWH lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you' (ASV 'as thy soul liveth'). The double oath is Elisha's own oath to Eliyahu at 2 Kgs 2:2, 4, 6, and is rendered identically: *ḥay-YHWH* 'As YHWH lives' (central `chei-x-oath-by-the-life-formula`), and *ḥê-nap̄šəḵā* 'as you yourself live' (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`). She repeats Elisha's words to Eliyahu, binding him as he once bound his master.

paragraphs.text: וְגֵחֲזִ֞י עָבַ֣ר לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם וַיָּ֤שֶׂם אֶת־הַמִּשְׁעֶ֙נֶת֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַנַּ֔עַר וְאֵ֥ין ק֖וֹל וְאֵ֣ין קָ֑שֶׁב וַיָּ֤שָׁב לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ וַיַּגֶּד־ל֣וֹ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א הֵקִ֖יץ הַנָּֽעַר׃

i18n.en: And Gechazi passed on before them and laid the staff on the face of the child; but there was no voice and no attention. And he went back to meet him and told him, saying, "The child has not awakened."

notes.official: *wəʾên qôl wəʾên qāšeḇ* 'but there was no voice and no attention' (ASV 'neither voice, nor hearing'), the phrase of 1 Kgs 18:29 for the silence of Ba'al, rendered there 'no one paying heed'. *lōʾ hēqîṣ hannaʿar* 'The child has not awakened': death described as sleep.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א אֱלִישָׁ֖ע הַבָּ֑יְתָה וְהִנֵּ֤ה הַנַּ֙עַר֙ מֵ֔ת מֻשְׁכָּ֖ב עַל־מִטָּתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Elisha came into the house, and behold, the child was dead, laid on his bed.

notes.official: *wəhinnēh hannaʿar mēṯ muškāḇ ʿal-miṭṭāṯô* 'and behold, the child was dead, laid on his bed'. The narrative leaves no doubt that the boy is dead (vv 20, 32), as in 1 Kgs 17:17. The Raëlian canon's citation runs from here to v 37 (see v 34).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיִּסְגֹּ֥ר הַדֶּ֖לֶת בְּעַ֣ד שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And he went in and shut the door on the two of them, and prayed to YHWH.

notes.official: *wayyisgōr haddeleṯ bəʿaḏ šənêhem wayyiṯpallēl ʾel-YHWH* 'and shut the door on the two of them, and prayed to YHWH': as in 1 Kgs 17:20-21, prayer precedes the physical act, and the narrative attributes the outcome to YHWH.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֜עַל וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב עַל־הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַיָּשֶׂם֩ פִּ֨יו עַל־פִּ֜יו וְעֵינָ֤יו עַל־עֵינָיו֙ וְכַפָּ֣יו עַל־כפו [כַּפָּ֔יו] וַיִּגְהַ֖ר עָלָ֑יו וַיָּ֖חָם בְּשַׂ֥ר הַיָּֽלֶד׃

i18n.en: And he went up and lay upon the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his palms on his palms; and he crouched over him, and the flesh of the child grew warm.

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *kpw* 'his palm' (singular) / Qere *kappāyw* 'his palms' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

*wayyiškaḇ ʿal-hayyeleḏ wayyāśem pîw ʿal-pîw wəʿênāyw ʿal-ʿênāyw wəḵappāyw ʿal-kappāyw* 'and lay upon the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his palms on his palms': the plain sense is kept, with no medical or other interpretation in the line. *wayyiḡhar ʿālāyw* 'and he crouched over him' (ASV 'stretched himself upon him'). *gāhar* occurs only here, at v 35 and at 1 Kgs 18:42, where Eliyahu 'crouched down upon the earth'; HALOT gives 'bend down, crouch', and the Kings rendering is made uniform so that the two prophets' postures stay visibly linked (`gahar-crouch-over-kings`). *wayyāḥom bəśar hayyāleḏ* 'and the flesh of the child grew warm'. The scene parallels 1 Kgs 17:21, where Eliyahu stretches himself over the boy three times.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) cites vv 32-37 as a 'resurrection' in quotation marks: Elisha treats the child and brings him back to life, which the canon compares to mouth-to-mouth resuscitation and heart massage. The line renders the Hebrew lexically ('mouth on his mouth', 'crouched over him') and does not add a medical term; the reading is recorded here only.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֜שָׁב וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ בַּבַּ֗יִת אַחַ֥ת הֵ֙נָּה֙ וְאַחַ֣ת הֵ֔נָּה וַיַּ֖עַל וַיִּגְהַ֣ר עָלָ֑יו וַיְזוֹרֵ֤ר הַנַּ֙עַר֙ עַד־שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֔ים וַיִּפְקַ֥ח הַנַּ֖עַר אֶת־עֵינָֽיו׃

i18n.en: Then he turned back and walked in the house once this way and once that way, and went up and crouched over him; and the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.

notes.official: *wayyāšāḇ wayyēleḵ babbayiṯ ʾaḥaṯ hēnnâ wəʾaḥaṯ hēnnâ* 'Then he turned back and walked in the house once this way and once that way'. *wayyiḡhar ʿālāyw* 'and crouched over him' (see v 34; `gahar-crouch-over-kings`). *wayzôrēr hannaʿar ʿaḏ-šeḇaʿ pəʿāmîm* 'and the child sneezed seven times': *zrr* occurs only here, and 'sneeze' is the traditional sense (BDB; HALOT; cf. Job 41:10 *ʿăṭîšâ*); the LXX instead makes Elisha the subject of a sevenfold bending over the child. The MT and the ASV sense are kept. *wayyip̄qaḥ hannaʿar ʾeṯ-ʿênāyw* 'and the child opened his eyes'. The canon's reading of the whole scene is recorded at v 34.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֶל־גֵּיחֲזִ֗י וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ קְרָא֙ אֶל־הַשֻּׁנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את וַיִּקְרָאֶ֖הָ וַתָּב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑יו וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שְׂאִ֥י בְנֵֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And he called Gechazi and said, "Call this Shunammite." So he called her, and she came to him. And he said, "Take up your son."

notes.official: *śəʾî ḇənēḵ* 'Take up your son': the words echo 1 Kgs 17:23 ('See, your son lives').

paragraphs.text: וַתָּבֹא֙ וַתִּפֹּ֣ל עַל־רַגְלָ֔יו וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָ֑רְצָה וַתִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת־בְּנָ֖הּ וַתֵּצֵֽא׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Then she came and fell at his feet and bowed herself to the ground; and she took up her son and went out.

notes.official: *wattippōl ʿal-raḡlāyw wattištaḥû ʾārṣâ* 'Then she came and fell at his feet and bowed herself to the ground' (ASV). The Hishtaphel of *ḥwh* is rendered by context in Kings ('bowed herself' here; 'worshipped' / 'bow down' at 17:16, 35, 36); the Genesis-scoped central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship` ('made obeisance') is not imported. The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) closes the episode.

paragraphs.text: וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב הַגִּלְגָּ֙לָה֙ וְהָרָעָ֣ב בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּבְנֵי֙ הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים יֹשְׁבִ֖ים לְפָנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְנַעֲר֗וֹ שְׁפֹת֙ הַסִּ֣יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֔ה וּבַשֵּׁ֥ל נָזִ֖יד לִבְנֵ֥י הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃

i18n.en: And Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was famine in the land; and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. And he said to his servant, "Set on the great pot, and boil stew for the sons of the prophets."

notes.official: *wəhārāʿāḇ bāʾāreṣ* 'and there was famine in the land' (cf. 8:1). *ûḇənê hannəḇîʾîm yōšəḇîm ləp̄ānāyw* 'and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him', as disciples before a master (`bene-ha-neviim-sons-of-the-prophets-kings`; central `navi-first-occurrence-abraham`). *nāzîḏ* 'stew', the word of Gen 25:29, where genesis-woh keeps the ASV 'pottage'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּצֵ֨א אֶחָ֣ד אֶל־הַשָּׂדֶה֮ לְלַקֵּ֣ט אֹרֹת֒ וַיִּמְצָא֙ גֶּ֣פֶן שָׂדֶ֔ה וַיְלַקֵּ֥ט מִמֶּ֛נּוּ פַּקֻּעֹ֥ת שָׂדֶ֖ה מְלֹ֣א בִגְד֑וֹ וַיָּבֹ֗א וַיְפַלַּ֛ח אֶל־סִ֥יר הַנָּזִ֖יד כִּֽי־לֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ׃

i18n.en: And one went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered from it wild gourds, his lap full, and came and sliced them into the pot of stew; for they did not know them.

notes.official: *ʾōrōṯ* 'herbs' (ASV; a rare word, perhaps 'mallows' or edible greens). *gep̄en śāḏeh* 'a wild vine' and *paqquʿōṯ śāḏeh* 'wild gourds', usually identified as the colocynth (*Citrullus colocynthis*), a bitter, purgative and in quantity poisonous gourd (Zohary 1982). *paqquʿōṯ* is from the same root as the gourd ornaments *pəqāʿîm* of the Temple (1 Kgs 6:18), which the Kings line now also renders 'gourds' (1-kings-woh overlay `peqaim-gourd-ornaments-1-kings-6`). *məlōʾ ḇiḡḏô* 'his lap full' (lit. 'his garment full').

paragraphs.text: וַיִּֽצְק֥וּ לַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים לֶאֱכ֑וֹל וַ֠יְהִי כְּאָכְלָ֨ם מֵהַנָּזִ֜יד וְהֵ֣מָּה צָעָ֗קוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ מָ֤וֶת בַּסִּיר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ לֶאֱכֹֽל׃

i18n.en: And they poured it out for the men to eat. And it came to pass, as they were eating of the stew, that they cried out and said, "There is death in the pot, O man of the Elohim!" And they could not eat it.

notes.official: *māweṯ bassîr ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm* 'There is death in the pot, O man of the Elohim!' (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ וּקְחוּ־קֶ֔מַח וַיַּשְׁלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־הַסִּ֑יר וַיֹּ֗אמֶר צַ֤ק לָעָם֙ וְיֹאכֵ֔לוּ וְלֹ֥א הָיָ֛ה דָּבָ֥ר רָ֖ע בַּסִּֽיר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: But he said, "Then bring flour." And he threw it into the pot and said, "Pour out for the people, that they may eat." And there was nothing harmful in the pot.

notes.official: *ûqəḥû-qemaḥ* 'Then bring flour': as with the salt at 2 Kgs 2:20-21, an ordinary substance is the means of the cure. *wəlōʾ hāyâ dāḇār rāʿ bassîr* 'And there was nothing harmful in the pot'.

paragraphs.text: וְאִ֨ישׁ בָּ֜א מִבַּ֣עַל שָׁלִ֗שָׁה וַיָּבֵא֩ לְאִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים לֶ֤חֶם בִּכּוּרִים֙ עֶשְׂרִֽים־לֶ֣חֶם שְׂעֹרִ֔ים וְכַרְמֶ֖ל בְּצִקְלֹנ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר תֵּ֥ן לָעָ֖ם וְיֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

i18n.en: And a man came from Ba'al-Shalishah and brought the man of the Elohim bread of the first-fruits, twenty loaves of barley, and fresh ears of grain in his sack. And he said, "Give to the people, that they may eat."

notes.official:
*mibbaʿal šālišâ* 'from Ba'al-Shalishah', a town in the hill country of Efrayim (cf. 1 Sam 9:4 'the land of Shalishah'). *leḥem bikkûrîm ʿeśrîm-leḥem śəʿōrîm* 'bread of the first-fruits, twenty loaves of barley': first-fruits were due to YHWH and the priests (Lev 23:20; Num 18:13; Deut 18:4); bringing them to the man of the Elohim treats the prophet as the recipient of sacred dues (Cogan and Tadmor). *wəḵarmel bəṣiqlōnô* 'and fresh ears of grain in his sack': *karmel* is fresh or new grain (Lev 2:14; 23:14), the same word as the name of Mount Karmel (v 25); *ṣiqlôn* occurs only here, 'sack, bag' (ASV, NJPS). 'the man of the Elohim' (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes vv 42-44 under the heading 'The multiplication of the loaves' ('twenty loaves of barley ... They shall eat, and shall leave thereof'). The line renders the Hebrew as the ASV does; the canon's reading is recorded here only.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ מְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ מָ֚ה אֶתֵּ֣ן זֶ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י מֵ֣אָה אִ֑ישׁ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר תֵּ֤ן לָעָם֙ וְיֹאכֵ֔לוּ כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה אָכֹ֥ל וְהוֹתֵֽר׃

i18n.en: And his attendant said, "How shall I set this before a hundred men?" But he said, "Give to the people, that they may eat; for thus says YHWH, 'They shall eat and have some left over.'"

notes.official: *məšārəṯô* 'his attendant' (ASV 'his servant'): *məšārēṯ* is a different word from *naʿar* (v 12) and is rendered 'attendant' to keep the two apart; it is the title of Yehoshua as Moshe's assistant (Ex 24:13) and of Elisha as Eliyahu's (1 Kgs 19:21 *wayšārəṯēhû*). *mēʾâ ʾîš* 'a hundred men'. *kōh ʾāmar YHWH ʾāḵōl wəhôṯēr* 'thus says YHWH, "They shall eat and have some left over"': two infinitives absolute, an oracular style ('eating and leaving over'); the ASV sense is kept. The story is the model for the feeding narratives of the Gospels (Mark 6:35-44; John 6:9, with barley loaves).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתֵּ֧ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֛ם וַיֹּאכְל֥וּ וַיּוֹתִ֖רוּ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of YHWH.

notes.official: *wayyōʾḵəlû wayyôṯirû kiḏḇar YHWH* 'and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of YHWH': the fulfilment repeats the oracle verb for verb. The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) closes the chapter. For the canon's reading of vv 42-44 see v 42.
